title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1971-07-02

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear FM broadcast captures a high‑energy Fillmore West show with a smoking Good Lovin’/Cryptical>Drums>Other One suite and blistering guitar work.
ai_review.review: The July 2, 1971 Fillmore West set is hailed as one of ’71’s finest – the band rides a raging wave of energy, delivering a monster Good Lovin’, an epic Cryptical‑Drums‑Other One sequence, and standout moments from Loser, Hard To Handle and Johnny B. Goode.  The FM broadcast source is remarkably clear, with occasional early‑set drop‑outs but overall excellent fidelity that lets the raw power of the performance shine through.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews, the vast majority rate the show 4‑5 stars and praise both the musical intensity and the clear FM broadcast; only a few low‑rating outliers mention tuning issues, so the combined weighted score is very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners repeatedly describe the FM broadcast as crystal‑clear and wonderful; a handful note minor early‑set dropouts or occasional muddiness, but overall the mix is praised for its clarity, balance, and inclusion of station IDs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The first half is a bit unfocused and out‑of‑tune, but the band launches into a high‑octane second set that builds to a climactic Other One suite; the closing feels like a historic Fillmore West send‑off.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for blazing guitar tone on Good Lovin', railroad blues solo, and overall fiery lead work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “hot Phil” bass on Loser and a powerful low‑end; some reviewers link his new Guild/Alembic bass to early tuning hiccups.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned missing the first few lines of "Playing in the Band" but otherwise praised his vocal energy; his rhythm work helps drive the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy Kreutzmann’s drumming is highlighted as tight, funky and propulsive, especially during the Other One suite; Bill Graham’s intro is also noted.
